policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 2 Apr close (1x4 3.82, 3x6 3.96, 6x9 4.13, 9x12 4.27 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 40bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar (a 'hawkish cut'); the 8-9 Apr meeting is expected to hold. Kotecki (2 Apr): the March cut was the last this year; Litwiniuk (2 Apr): no cuts soon, hikes possible if inflation worsens. March flash CPI 3.0% (31 Mar; 3.3% expected); core 2.5% in February. The fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise) takes ~0.9pp off April CPI (ING, PKO).
policy.risk_text: War and oil set the direction: FRAs price NBP hikes the MPC says it does not plan; escalation would lift the front end further, a ceasefire would unwind hike pricing. Long end: global term premia (Bund ~3%) and the fiscal cost of the fuel shield.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026 (Inflation Report, 6 Mar); the NBP forecaster survey (1 Apr) has 2026 CPI at 2.9%. The next projection comes in July.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.2% of GDP (GUS preliminary, 1 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; S&P (2-6 Apr) sees a 2026 deficit of 7.0% of GDP (8.0% in an oil-shock case); budget deficit after February PLN 48.5bn; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) from 27-31 Mar.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~41% (end-Q1) financed; budget accounts ~PLN 167bn at end-March (MoF estimate). No rating action in April; S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar (next MPC 8-9 Apr); March CPI 3.0% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 4.0%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 2-6 Apr: Kotecki said the March cut was the last this year and Litwiniuk ruled out near-term cuts, with hikes possible if inflation worsens (2 Apr); S&P raised its 2026 deficit forecast for Poland to 7.0% of GDP (8.0% in an oil-shock case); FRAs priced ~50bp of 2026 NBP hikes (PKO); POLGBs rose only 1-3bp on 2 Apr; no bond sessions on 3 and 6 Apr (Easter). Abroad: Trump's address promised two-three more weeks of strikes and Brent jumped ~8% to ~$109; almost three ECB and two BoE hikes priced again; US payrolls +178k (60k expected) left ~1bp of 2026 Fed easing priced; Trump set an 8 Apr deadline for Iran.

calendar.plan_text: MoF April plan (31 Mar): sale auctions on 15 Apr (PLN 4-12bn; OK0128, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1035, NZ0936), 23 Apr (6-14bn) and 28 Apr (5-13bn; new 10Y DS0436 replaces DS1035 from 23 Apr); no switch; a 50-week T-bill on 10 Apr (3-6bn). Q2 plan: 7-8 sales for PLN 50-90bn and 1-2 switches. 2026 needs ~41% financed at end-Q1.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it. April is back to regular supply: remaining sales 15 Apr, 23 Apr, 28 Apr. MPC 8-9 Apr: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: war shock - oil above $100 and core yields near multi-year highs; the NBP is at 3.75% after the March cut while FRAs price roughly 40bp of NBP hikes; the ECB and BoE are priced for hikes, the Fed is on hold, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 65bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 275bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 2 Apr close). Payrolls +178k; Brent ~$109 after Trump's address (2-6 Apr).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK's Q2 FPC calendar (31 Mar) has tenders on 16 and 29 Apr, 14 and 28 May and 18 Jun; on 26 Mar it sold only PLN 0.87bn (demand 1.06bn) plus 0.20bn.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
